title: Arctiva — Linux, without the barriers.
description: Arctiva is an Arch Linux–based distribution with a graphical installer, KDE Plasma, automatic snapshots and gaming out of the box.
lead: A Linux distribution based on Arch Linux: the official Arch repositories and rolling releases, with a graphical installer, a familiar desktop and safe updates.
legal_independent: Arctiva is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Arch Linux.
legal_license: The code is released under GPL-3.0-or-later. The name and the logo are not covered by that license: they are governed by the project's trademark policy.
roadmap_more: Full detail in the project's roadmap.
about_p: Arctiva is for people coming from Windows, or who want Arch without building it by hand. It keeps the best of Arch — unmodified official repositories, pacman and rolling releases — and adds what Arch lacks for everyday use: a graphical installer, a KDE Plasma desktop that feels familiar, simple updates with automatic snapshots to go back to, and games and graphics drivers without the fuss.

principles.p: Official core, extra and multilib, untouched and on time. If something in Arch breaks, it is mitigated with warnings and snapshots, not with a fork.
[arctiva] holds only our own pieces and is signed with GPG. The master key stays offline; only continuous integration signs, never a personal machine.
The desktop is adapted through configuration and themes only. Plasma and Calamares are never modified, so updates don't break anything.
Each ISO pins a date of the Arch Linux Archive, so it can be rebuilt with exactly the same packages.
What doesn't work — Secure Boot, some anti-cheat games, certain Windows programs — is explained clearly.
All the code, design decisions and the roadmap are public on GitHub.

feat_h: Everything you need, in one system

feat.p: Try the full KDE Plasma desktop without installing anything, then install with a Calamares-based wizard with Arctiva's own design. Offline install: it copies the tested live system, so it is fast.
Btrfs with zstd compression. Snapper and snap-pac take a snapshot before and after every package change, and GRUB lets you boot any of them.
Menu, taskbar and tray like Windows from the first minute. Dolphin, high-refresh-rate screens (VRR), HDR; old X11 apps still work through Xwayland.
Before touching the disk, a check warns about hibernated Windows or Fast Startup and active BitLocker, and GRUB lists Windows automatically. Optional disk encryption asks the password only once.
AMD and Intel work out of the box. NVIDIA GTX 16 / RTX 20 and later are detected and get nvidia-open automatically. Older GTX 900/1000 use the free driver, and you are told your options.
multilib on by default; Steam, Lutris, GameMode, MangoHud and Gamescope in the Gaming profile. Heroic, ProtonPlus and Bottles are planned.
One native app (Python + Qt/PySide6) for updates, drivers and extras. The base window exists and is already published; its modules are being written.
A store with official repositories, Flathub and the AUR clearly told apart, plus Bottles for .exe and .msi files — with honest compatibility notes.

install_p: The graphical installer walks you through the whole process. Basic is always installed, with or without internet; extras are downloaded only when there is a connection.
snap_h: If an update breaks something, go back
snap_p: Arctiva takes a snapshot before every update. If something fails, reboot, pick the previous snapshot in the GRUB menu and your system works again.

snap_lines.t: After the reboot, something is broken.

profiles.p: Plasma desktop, Firefox, snapshots and everything needed to start. Always installed.
Steam, Lutris, GameMode, MangoHud and Gamescope, with the 32-bit graphics libraries.
LibreOffice and Thunderbird in English, Spanish and Catalan, with spell checkers, compatible fonts, and scanner and printer support.

center_p: One app that brings Arctiva's tools together, with the look of Plasma. In development (phase 4, version 0.5.0).

center.p: Reads the archlinux.org news since your last update and blocks the update until you read any item that needs manual action. Flags delicate packages (kernel, NVIDIA, Mesa, systemd, Plasma), updates Flatpaks, and helps with .pacnew files.
Translates the usual failures — conflicts, keys, disk space, no network — into clear messages, without hiding the original text.
Shows the detected graphics card and what is missing, and installs it.
Gaming, Office, LTS kernel, printers and firewall: install and remove with one toggle.
Admin actions go through a helper with a closed set of operations — never arbitrary commands — and ask for the password with the standard system dialog (polkit).
When GRUB is updated it is also reinstalled on the EFI partition, so your machine is never left unable to boot.

roadmap.t: Signed [arctiva] repository, graphics detection. Almost done.
GRUB theme, boot screen, login, Plasma theme, wallpapers.

reqs: 40 GB of disk (64 GB recommended, because of snapshots)
USB drive of 8 GB or more
limits: UEFI only; old BIOS machines are not supported.
NVIDIA GTX 900/1000 use the free driver by default.
Some anti-cheat games and some Windows programs do not work.
noiso_p: Arctiva is in development, before its first beta. If you want to try it, you can build the ISO from the source code.
